faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before getting started.

q1.question: How does the platform work?
q1.answer: You create your organization, invite your team and configure your product. Auth, billing and multi-tenancy are ready: start from day one.

q2.question: Do I need technical skills?
q2.answer: Customizing the branding takes a few environment variables. Extending the product requires knowing Nuxt and TypeScript.

q3.question: Is it really multi-tenant?
q3.answer: Yes. Every account is an organization and every resource is isolated per tenant. The model is B2B-first with B2C as a special case.

q4.question: Is my data safe?
q4.answer: Absolutely. We use standard encryption, are GDPR compliant and support data export and deletion on request.

q5.question: Can I try before paying?
q5.answer: Join the waiting list to get priority access and a lifetime discount. Early users also get one month of Premium free.

q6.question: When will it be available?
q6.answer: We are working on the launch. Join the waiting list to be among the first to try the platform and get updates.

chiSiamo.seoDescription: Ceremly was born in 2026 in Milan, out of a wedding organized with spreadsheets. Digital invitations and RSVPs built for events.
chiSiamo.heroSub: Ceremly was born in 2026, in Milan, out of a wedding organized with spreadsheets, voice notes and calls to the mother-in-law.
chiSiamo.intro1: The idea came from a wedding: three days before the party, the caterer called with three different numbers on three different sheets. The invitations had been beautiful. The guest list, a nightmare. You wonder why in 2026 you can book a flight in two minutes, but not know how many uncles are coming to lunch.
chiSiamo.intro2: So Ceremly was built: digital invitations that hold their own next to paper ones, and a reply form anyone can use — no app, no account, no explaining over the phone. Today it's in beta, small by choice, growing one event at a time.

principi.d: No gift registries, no albums, no showcase sites. Ceremly answers one question — who's coming? — and that's it. What we don't do is a choice, not a gap.

principi.t: The data belongs to the hosts
principi.d: Guest lists are never sold, profiled, or fed into ads. EU servers, full export anytime, real deletion when you ask for it.
Italian events, Italian etiquette, Italian e-invoicing. We build for how people celebrate here: big families, late confirmations and long lunches.

team.d: Watched a wedding run on spreadsheets and decided to build the alternative. Never again.

chiSiamo.ctaSub: The best way to get to know us is to use Ceremly for your next event.

comeFunziona.seoTitle: How Ceremly works — from invitation to final guest list
comeFunziona.seoDescription: Four steps to know who's coming to your event: create the invitation, import your list, share it, and collect replies. Without chasing anyone.
comeFunziona.heroTitlePart1: From first draft to final list,
comeFunziona.heroSub: Four steps. The first takes five minutes; the other three work on their own while you focus on the event.

steps.t: Pick a template, make it yours.
steps.d: Wedding, graduation, christening or birthday: start from a curated template and change the colours, photos and text. No design skills needed.
bullets: Date, venue and dress code included

steps.d: Paste it from Excel or your contacts. Ceremly spots duplicates and lets you group guests by family, side or table.

steps.t: One link. Or a hundred personal invites.
steps.d: Drop a single link in the group chat, or send each guest their own named invitation by WhatsApp and email. A QR code for anyone still on paper.

steps.t: The replies come in on their own.
steps.d: Confirmations, menus, allergies and plus-ones land in your dashboard as they arrive. Latecomers get gentle, automatic reminders.
bullets: Menu and allergies in the form

comeFunziona.ctaSub: Create your first invitation in five minutes. Thirty guests free, forever.

funzionalita.seoTitle: Ceremly features — one problem, solved well
funzionalita.seoDescription: Invitations that are a joy to open, frictionless RSVPs and a dashboard that answers one question: who's coming? Explore everything Ceremly does.
funzionalita.heroSub: Ceremly doesn't do wedding websites, gift registries or photo albums. It does one thing: tells you who's really coming to your event.

groups.title: A joy to open
groups.desc: First impressions count: the invitation is the cover of your event.

feats.d: Weddings, graduations, christenings and birthdays — curated and ready in five minutes.
Customise the palette and images. With Celebration, even your event's own colours.
Love a printed invitation? The QR code still leads to the digital reply form.

groups.title: Frictionless RSVPs
groups.desc: The easier it is to reply, the sooner your list is closed.

feats.d: Open the link, reply. No sign-up, no app to download.
The form gathers everything you and the caterer need, in one go.
Gentle nudges to anyone who hasn't replied, at the pace you choose.

groups.title: Everything in hand
groups.desc: The dashboard answers the only question that matters: who's coming?

feats.d: One invitation per household, individual replies. Adults and children counted separately.
Opens, confirmations, trends. You always know where you stand.
Final list with menus and allergies, as CSV or PDF, ready to forward.

funzionalita.ctaSub: Thirty guests and one active event on the Free plan. Forever.

modelli.seoTitle: Invitation templates — start out beautiful with Ceremly
modelli.seoDescription: Six families of templates for weddings, graduations, christenings and birthdays. Everything customisable: colours, photos, text and reply form.
modelli.heroSub: Six families of templates, each designed for an occasion. Everything is customisable: colours, photos, text and the reply form.
modelli.noteText: Three templates included on the Free plan. Every template and made-to-measure colours from the Celebration plan.

prezzi.seoTitle: Ceremly pricing — thirty guests free, forever
prezzi.seoDescription: Free to get started, Celebration as a one-off payment per event, Atelier for professional organisers. Compare Ceremly's plans and features.

faq.q: Can I start free and move to Celebration later?
faq.a: Yes. Everything you've created — invitation, list, replies — stays put. You simply unlock the limits when you need them.
The event stays available for 12 months: list, replies and exports included. After that you can archive it or download everything.
No: it's a one-off payment per event. No renewals, no surprises. Only Atelier, built for professional organisers, is monthly.

guidaRsvp.seoTitle: RSVP guide: how to actually get replies
guidaRsvp.seoDescription: Répondez s'il vous plaît, done right. When to send invitations, how to word the request, and how to handle stragglers so your numbers are solid.
guidaRsvp.heroSub: Répondez s'il vous plaît: how to ask guests to confirm — and actually get them to. A ten-minute read.
toc: What RSVP is (and why it gets ignored)
When to send and when to close
guidaRsvp.s1Title: What RSVP is (and why it gets ignored)
guidaRsvp.s1p1: RSVP is the request to confirm your attendance. It sounds trivial, but roughly one guest in three never replies on their own — not out of rudeness, but because the request is vague, has no deadline, or is buried in a 40-person group chat.
guidaRsvp.s1p2: The good news: RSVP isn't an etiquette problem, it's a process problem. And processes can be fixed.
guidaRsvp.s2Title: When to send and when to close
guidaRsvp.s2p1: The golden rule: work backwards from the date your caterer needs final numbers. For a wedding, the typical timeline looks like this:

timeline.title: Send the invitations
timeline.desc: Two months ahead for weddings, two weeks for birthdays and graduations.

timeline.title: First reminder
timeline.desc: A gentle nudge to anyone who hasn't opened or replied yet.

timeline.title: Second reminder
timeline.desc: More direct: the deadline is close, and it's for you, not for them.

timeline.title: Close the list
timeline.desc: Numbers frozen: the export goes out to caterer and venue.

guidaRsvp.s2p2: For graduations and birthdays, compress everything: invite two weeks ahead, reminder at one week, close three days out.
guidaRsvp.s3p1: Three ingredients, always: an explicit deadline ("by July 1st"), a single action (one link, not "let me know"), and a personal tone (the guest's name does half the work).
guidaRsvp.exampleText: "Hi Marta! We're getting married on September 12th in Cernobbio 💍 Here's the invitation with all the details: ceremly.it/giulia-tommaso — confirm by July 1st so we can give the caterer our numbers. Hugs!"
guidaRsvp.s3p2: Notice what's missing: apologies, preambles, "whenever you can". The kindness is in the tone, not in the vagueness.
guidaRsvp.s4p1: There will always be some. The trick is not to chase them by hand: set up automatic reminders and let "the system" do the insisting — a nudge from a platform weighs less than three messages from you.
guidaRsvp.s4p2: For the truly stubborn, the final week is worth a phone call. By then it'll be five people, not fifty: which is exactly the point.
guidaRsvp.ctaSub: Deadlines, reminders and exports are already in the product. You just write the invitation.

cookie.intro: In short: we use four cookies, all our own. No advertising tracking, no third parties, so no endless banners.

rows.name: ceremly_rsvp
rows.purpose: Remembers the guest's reply on their device

sections.t: What they are and how we use them
ps: Cookies are small files saved by your browser. Ceremly uses them only for essential functions (keeping you signed in, remembering a guest's reply) and for anonymous statistics computed on our own servers — we use no third-party analytics tools or advertising pixels.

Essential cookies require no consent and the service won't work without them. Preference and statistics cookies can be declined from the banner on first visit, or disabled anytime from your browser settings.
If you block all cookies in your browser, invitation pages remain viewable but the reply won't be remembered on the device.
If we introduce new cookies we'll update this page and, where required, the consent banner.
